Abul Bashar Bhuiyan, Advocate — For the Petitioner. 
Kaiseruddin Ahmed, Deputy Attorney-General — For the Respondents.
parties:
Abul Hasnat Md and Serajudoula Bhuiyan ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 2. It is stated by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that this detenu was convicted in a case numbering 5(5) and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months under sections 467/468/420/471 of the Penal Code. He was arrested on 4-11-95. So the period of six months is already over. In the affidavit-in-opposition it is stated that this detenu was brought to Dhaka Central Jail on 4-1-96 and he was convicted and sentenced to suffer one year's rigorous imprisonment in Case No. P-No. 151(A)1986 under sections 323/373 of the Penal Code on 19-2-96 by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. It appears that the period of one year also expired in view of the fact that the sentence was awarded to him on 19-2-96. In the affidavit-in-opposition the learned Deputy Attorney-General further stated that on 22-1-96 he was detained as under trial prisoner in view of the fact that the Panchlaish PS Case No. 17(7)/1980 (CR 1114/1980) under sections 143/448/384 BPC and Panchlaish PS Case No. 5(5)/1981 under sections 467/468/420/471 BPC are pending. The learned Advocate for the petitioner finds it difficult to challenge this statement of the State in view of the fact that he could not collect any paper with regard to the aforesaid case. But he submits that his instruction is that in both the cases the detenu has been discharged. Further, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has submitted a certificate issued by the Resident Physician of Pabna Mental Hospital dated 2-5-95 showing that the detenu is a mental patient and he was given treatment in that hospital. Further, the resident physician suggested for treatment of the detenu in Dhaka Medical College Hospital or PG Hospital as out-door patient in the concerned department. It is further stated that the detenu is in Chittagong District Jail. Be that as it may, since it is alleged that the two criminal cases are pending in Chittagong Court, we should direct the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, to look into the matter as to whether actually the two criminal cases are pending or not. If the two criminal cases are pending in Chittagong Magistrate Court, the detenu should be treated as under trial prisoner and he shall be enlarged on bail to the satisfaction of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong as the detenu is a mental patient. If it is found that he was discharged from the aforesaid Panchlaish PS Cases then the detenu will be released from jail. With the above direction this Rule is disposed of.
